summary.headline: Patanjali Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to INR11,337 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR543 crore (4.80% margin).
summary.overview:
Management reported the fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue, led by edible oils (INR8,505 crore, record) and oil palm (INR740 crore, up 25% YoY). FMCG revenue was INR2,938 crore at a 6.45% EBITDA margin, with biscuits and HPC growing strongly while staples were loss-making at INR-59 crore EBITDA. Input inflation from delayed monsoon and West Asia conflict was a net positive for edible oils (long positions) but a headwind for FMCG. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, while flagging caution on staples demand and margins.</overview>

segments.name: Edible oil
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8,505 crore, record, led by mustard oil; EBITDA margin 5.22%. Veg oil inflation helped as the company is long edible oils.

segments.name: Oil palm plantation
segments.commentary: Revenue INR740 crore, up 25% YoY. Cultivated area 1,15,861 ha as of 30 June 2026 against 6.63 lakh ha allocated; about 37% in the 7-25 year prime yielding phase.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Revenue INR560 crore, up 27% YoY, EBITDA margin 15.35% vs 9.35%. Doodh Biscuit (INR5 and INR10 packs) is cited at about INR1,300 crore annual business.

segments.name: Textured soya (Nutrela)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR160 crore, up 14% YoY and 50% QoQ, EBITDA margin above 18%. Management cites about 40% market share.

segments.name: Ghee
segments.commentary: Revenue INR219 crore, softer on seasonal demand and lower Middle East off-take amid geopolitical disruption.

segments.name: Beverages
segments.commentary: Revenue INR38 crore, helped by extended summer and launches of mango chutney, mango panna juice and orange juice.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR18 crore; management says the segment has turned EBITDA-positive from earlier marginal losses, with sports nutrition gaining momentum.

segments.name: Home & Personal Care
segments.commentary: Revenue INR629 crore: dental INR325 crore, skin care INR165 crore, home care INR83 crore, hair care and others INR56 crore. Skin care was the main growth driver.

segments.name: Staples and ethnic foods
segments.commentary: Staples revenue above INR1,000 crore with EBITDA of INR-59 crore; ethnic foods (honey, dry fruits, spices, herbal etc.) revenue INR203 crore with EBITDA INR9 crore.

guidance_outlook: Full-year edible oil volume growth of 3% to 5%, with edible oil margin construct of 3% to 5% (also cited as 2% to 4% later in the call).
Food and FMCG growth of 8% to 10%; beauty and personal care growing around 15%.
FMCG vertical EBITDA growth of 12% to 15% for the year; later described as 10% to 12% EBITDA growth overall.
Textured soya margin guided at 16% to 18%, with management expecting to stay above 18%.
FMCG revenue expected to reach about INR12,500 crore this year from about INR11,000 crore+ last year (CEO estimate).
Oil palm business expected to grow more than 15% this year.
Management aims for EBITDA of about INR2,500 crore over the next 18 months on an annualised basis (CEO view, not formal guidance).
E-commerce and quick commerce plus modern trade targeted to rise from about 15% to 20% of revenue within 18 months.
capex_capacity: Oil palm cultivated area 1,15,861 ha as of 30 June 2026 out of 6.63 lakh ha allocated under the National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm.
No capex or new capacity figures were discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Foods volume grew about 5% YoY and pricing about 12% (management corrected an earlier approximation of 7-8% volume growth).
Calibrated price increases taken in edible oils; targeted discounts in FMCG; smaller pack sizes introduced. Pricing measures continue in Q2.
Palm oil prices firmed from March 2026, eased late in the quarter, then recovered to a two-week high in mid-August; rupee depreciated about 2.5%.
Soya oil futures rose about 40% by end-March, then stabilised; FOB prices corrected 6%.
Milk and sugar prices firmed; wheat stable. Packaging, freight and logistics costs rose in the quarter.
Management cautious on staples: El Nino food inflation uncertainty and rural demand stress; staples expected to see the most rural pressure in Q2.
Dishwash: management says no plans to exit or slow down, with variant launches continuing as the MNC exits.
